transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I’m here because I keep blowing up at people over nothing. I yelled at one of my employees for putting stock on the wrong shelf, and afterward I was shaking. That’s not how I usually treat people.
Between these moments when you blow up, how has your mood been generally?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to my mood in between, honestly.
About how often are these blow-ups happening?
More often than I’d like—several times lately. It can be over really small things, like the stock being put on the wrong shelf.
About how long ago did you first start having these kinds of outbursts?
About two weeks now—since the kitchen fire, that first weekend we were working on the house.
Since the fire, have you been having unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about it?

Yeah. It just pops into my head without warning. I’ll be doing something normal, like picking up a pan or opening a spreadsheet, and suddenly I can smell the smoke and see the kitchen filling up again. It’s like I’m right back there for a second.
About how long ago did the kitchen fire happen?
About two weeks ago, during that first weekend we were working on the house.
Have you been actively avoiding thoughts, places, or things that remind you of the fire?

Yes. I’ve been avoiding the house, and I can’t even look at the mortgage folder. Even the herbs on my patio make my chest tighten because they remind me of that day. I just can’t make myself go near those things.
